metadata.name: whereis
metadata.displayName: whereis - Locate binary, source, and man page
metadata.description: Locate the binary, source, and manual page for a command

installation.note: whereis is commonly available by default on Linux systems

overview.summary: whereis locates the binary (executable), source code, and manual page files for a given command name. It searches only in standard directories (PATH for binaries, MANPATH for man pages, etc.), so it is fast and predictable.
when_to_use: Find where a command's executable is installed
Find the man page path for a command
Check if a command is installed and where

syntax.description: NAME is the program name (e.g., ls, grep). whereis looks for binaries, man pages, and source in standard locations.

examples.title: Find all locations for a command
examples.description: Show binary, man page, and source paths for ls
examples.use_case: See where a command and its docs live

examples.title: Find only the binary
examples.description: Show only the grep executable path(s)
examples.use_case: Get the full path for scripting

related_commands.description: Shows only the executable used in PATH (one per name)
Fast filename search across the whole system (database)
